title: Python SDK
bodyMarkdown:
## Use the local adapter

Select the qualified cq-sdk package first. Run this canonical fragment inside your application async context, with an authenticated executable digest and an existing payments workload.

```python
from cq import LocalCLIClient, RunStdio

cq = LocalCLIClient(
    executable="/absolute/operator-verified/cq",
    expected_sha256="<64 lowercase hexadecimal characters from the release verification route>",
    config="/absolute/protected/cq.json",
    state_dir="/absolute/protected/cq-state",
    environment={},
)

review = await cq.config_get("/workloads/payments")
await cq.config_set(
    "/workloads/payments/environment",
    {"APP_MODE": "production"},
    expect_sha256=review["sha256"],
)
await cq.run("payments", stdio=RunStdio.INHERIT)
```

The environment starts empty. The reviewed SHA guards the change; on conflict inspect the new policy before retrying. run requires the explicit RunStdio.INHERIT selection because child output may contain values. Caller cancellation is re-raised after the owned child is reaped.

## Handle results and choose MCP

Handle safe error categories and propagate cancellation through your application. Do not log raw values or repeat an uncertain action merely because a client timed out. For MCP, create and authenticate the official session yourself, then use the language adapter shown in the canonical README. Session authentication does not grant provider access or plaintext disclosure. Source examples are not proof of package publication or live-provider qualification.
capabilityStatus: The Python local adapter invokes an explicitly verified native executable; running a workload explicitly inherits its standard streams. MCP requires an application-owned session. Installation does not grant provider or secret access.
